title: I Watched Every YT Quantum Computing Video — Decoding The Question If QC Is Here?
bodyHtml:
I Watched Every YT Quantum Computing Video — Decoding The Question If QC Is Here?

This series has finally come to an end. However, it was a very unplanned ending. As for this blog, I started looking for content last week! In that process, I ended up watching almost all the quantum computing content on YouTube based on the future, basics, and theoretical understanding, delving into some quantum mechanics, too. Apart from those, there is one other type of content on YouTube for quantum computing: tutorials on Quantum Platforms and lecture series by universities/communities, which I definitely skipped for everyone’s betterment…

We basically talked about qubits and quantum circuits/hardware in comparison with the classical counterpart, not delving too deep but just enough to build a mindset that can research and get started on this topic. Obviously, I wanted to talk a lot more on the topic, but I don’t like to write long blogs, which end up on reading lists rather than being read or complex blogs with zero context and connection throughout the series, so this blog will focus on debunking the question: “IS QUANTUM COMPUTING HERE?”.

Tri-Binaries of this Industry

Watching so many world leaders speak on TED Talks, or podcasts coming from different regions of the world or different backgrounds, it was very sad to see similar kinds of content flowing around. Listening to these people, I realized something — that I could categorize them into a tri-binary map of my own:

1st Level of Classification: Computing vs Technology
Quantum Computing and Quantum Technologies are 2 completely different fields! Computing covers all the hardware, software, error correction, fault tolerance, QPU, and all the competing stuff only which we already know. However, Quantum Technology delves into more than that; it is a kind of research field where we try to uncover other ways to use the same fundamental Quantum Mechanical Laws, which are the roots of all quantum-related stuff (as mentioned in the map, QUANTUM).

Some examples of Quantum Technology are quantum sensors used for various research purposes, quantum communication to secure our methods of communication post-quantum, and sometimes even nanotechnology. Though it is not using quantum at the moment, it will in the future. Quantum Chemistry also falls under the Quantum Technology use-cases branch, where we simulate chemicals and molecules to progress scientific innovations.

2nd Level of Classification: Applied vs Theoretical
Here we will find the answer to the question, “Where is Quantum now? And when will it arrive?” If I were a stand-up comedian, I would say, ‘It has already left its starting point, but I can only answer either the speed at which it is coming or its position!” You will get it after the explanation below, and even then, you won’t laugh because I am not a stand-up comedian.

This classification describes the 2 major fields of study in quantum computing, but before we move forward, here’s a small recap on why is there quantum computing in the first place! It all started with Feynman, who wanted to simulate reality to understand it better and use it in so many different ways, so from this story, we can conclude that he wasn’t going to make a quantum computer for commercial use like we see today.

It is still not commercial; however, frameworks like Qiskit allow individuals and companies to use the power of a quantum computer for specific use cases like Machine Learning, Drug Discovery, executing different algorithms, or research. Now, please understand that Applied still means research however, research in engineering parts of the quantum computer or working on solving the problems we face in quantum computing today, whereas Theoretical field studies on improving quantum computers for the future, or the research of finding more use-cases to boost the value of this technology, developing algorithms is also theoretical aspect as running those algorithms today won’t lead to any major results and will require significantly many more qubits and noise-tolerance to even run which the modern quantum computers lack.

So, how does this settle the debate? And what is the meaning of the joke? Well, the joke was based on Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle, which many of us might know: there is a limit to the precision of determining the 2 physical properties, position & momentum, of a particle, the answer to this debate much like the principle is divided into 2 schools of thought equally right in their approach leading to no conclusion. As we discussed, quantum computing was never intended for public use like classical computing, and hence, when we currently see quantum computing being used in the industry for research. Scientists might argue that Quantum is already here but not as efficient. They say this on a technicality that quantum is definitely being used, so it is here, though it is not efficient, which both parties agree. There is not only a room but a huge castle for improvement at this early stage of development.

However, engineers, entrepreneurs, salesmen, or any other regular Joe would feel that Quantum isn’t here, and they might be talking about the commercial use of this technology, which is definitely not here!

So, how do we settle the debate? Actually, there is a very clever idea proposed by John Preskill, which we all might’ve heard of but not actually understood completely, QUANTUM SUPREMACY! However, we’ll talk about it after the last classification.

3rd Level of Classification: Computing vs Devices
The computing you see here isn’t the same as the 1st classification, as the first focuses on the betterment of quantum computing by building better quantum computers, whereas this computing is where we explore use cases collaborating with quantum computers. So, Quantum Machine Learning, Quantum AI, Drug Discovery using QC, and Quantum Chemistry all fall under this category. There is actually sufficient research going on to improve stock market predictions using Quantum Computers as well, so even that falls under this category. The first Computing classification covers all the QEC, Quantum Fault-Tolernece, handling Noise, and increasing the number of qubits research, which works within the confines of improving quantum computers.

Quantum devices are a very new field of research covering quantum sensors we talked about, and quantum communication falls under this category, which uses very little or no help from Quantum Computers but is a totally different technology using quantum mechanics. However, that isn’t the case every time, as there is a unique product named Quokka launched by Chris Ferrie, a famous author on Quantum Computing and Quantum Physics. This product is related to quantum computing however, doesn’t make use of either quantum mechanics or a quantum computer but actually uses classical computing to emulate a quantum computer which can be said to fall under this category as well.

QUANTUM SUPREMACY

This topic has created so much nuisance in the YT world and in the industry despite being known about, like any other technical term, having only hype around it with no sufficient understanding!!!

Google has been using this term a lot when showcasing its Quantum achievements, and here’s what it actually means for everyone to understand. There are 3 things to keep in mind when dealing with Quantum Supremacy:

1. Qubits v/s QuBits
Quantum Supremacy marks the advantage of quantum computing against classical computing, so, naturally, our second blog of the series, Qubits vs Bits, handled that pretty well however, do not forget that even classical computers can simulate quantum computers, so given enough storage and process power if number of qubits in a quantum computer can be matched by a classical computer, the classical computer can far surpass the need of the quantum computer because classical simulation doesn’t need to deal with noise which is a major drawback when using quantum computers. So, there is no doubt about the accuracy of results that can be brought out with classical simulation, even though qubits have properties that surpass bits.

That’s why instead of Qubits vs Bits, it is Qubits of quantum computers vs QuBits of classical counterparts. If you understand this much, this is the first checkpoint of quantum supremacy. Now, you might ponder, why don’t we just use classical ones without bothering to make quantum computers, well the reason is that with technology getting better, even though we have much more storage and processing power than before, the ratio of bits required to simulate quantum bits is exponential (n:2^n) so, after a point even with the all the supercomputers in the world put together wouldn’t be able to simulate a quantum computer more than 100 qubits! Yes, imagine the number of bits required to simulate 100 qubits. It is well beyond the storage any existing supercomputer has, so that definitely marks the first checkpoint that we have already crossed with about 1180 qubits by Atom Computing on Oct 24, 2023, before the release of this blog.

2. Execution Accuracy
As we have already discussed, noise plays a major role when working with actual quantum computers, and though now, this is a preliminary test alongside the first checkpoint, I wanted to include it separately to shine a light on its importance because, without proper execution, you cannot say you have a working quantum computer and so, no matter the amount of qubits you make there is no point to it.

Said that there should be no doubt that we aren’t just talking about proper qubits but about the whole QPU/quantum circuit, meaning all the gates should be working accurately as well. If you understand what I am saying, you will understand why I had to make it a separate section. This is the testing phase as well as the building phase of the quantum circuit. Here, every logic gate is put to the test, and its accuracy is ensured. Now, talking about the first part of the section: Execution. Well, execution not only means that it works but also how long it works because qubits tend to lose their quantum state very quickly depending on the quality of the qubit. Many of the current working IBM quantum computers can only hold their quantum state up to a maximum of 70 to 80 microseconds, and the maximum recorded time till now again goes to Atom Computing, whose 1180 neutral-atom qubits can hold their state for nearly a minute.

Don’t get them WRONG! They aren’t worthless because of the minor time period they can hold because it is just like a Google search; even though Google has a massive database, it can still give results in many microseconds; such is the power of quantum computers as well; and they can carry out significant workload before they perish. They still aren’t that good, but even for microseconds of a lifetime, they produce sufficient results for research to advance.

3. Algorithm Threshold
This is the final checkpoint of quantum supremacy, which means you will finally understand why Google’s obsession with it. The qubit number, along with execution and accuracy, aren’t enough themselves because even with a quantum computer to surpass those tasks, they don’t necessarily show extraordinary results compared to classical computers. Remember, how we understood the fundamental difference between classical circuits and quantum circuits in our last blog? We ended on the note that simple arithmetic can be challenging for quantum computers. So, to demonstrate their final prowess against classical computers, they need to beat the execution time to run an algorithm by milestones against using classical computers. Actually, not only classical computers but actually supercomputers.

Here are a few examples of Google’s Quantum Supremacy claims:

  • Google’s Sycamore quantum processor solved a problem in 200 seconds that would have taken the world’s fastest supercomputer 10,000 years. (2019)
  • Google scientists are reporting that they completed a computational task on a quantum computer that would take a classical supercomputer 47 years to complete. (2023)

Note, if you understand the intricacies of Quantum Supremacy, you know this achievement can be fulfilled using a single task only, meaning even if once a quantum computer fulfills all 3 requirements, it is marked as quantum supremacy, which doesn’t necessarily mean that a quantum computer is faster than supercomputers in everything.

This blog first gave you insight into what quantum computing is and gave you a taste of different branches of quantum technologies. Second, you understand the practicality of the technology now and in the future, delving into 2 schools of thought. And lastly, we covered the pillar of determining any quantum computer’s worth, meaning the buzzword QUANTUM SUPREMACY.

The videos I saw on YouTube did not completely cover all these concepts when speaking about quantum computing’s existence, and hence by reading this blog, you can hopefully grasp the market’s situation for yourself and continue to learn more about this industry.

With all these concepts by your side, I leave it for you to decide whether to believe quantum computers are here or it is yet to become a part of our world!
